description:
The relationships that survive the most difficult periods are rarely the ones where nothing went wrong. They are the ones where something going wrong finally forced two people to become honest.

Rachel Pringle, sensual embodiment teacher and creator of the Wild Woman Experience, describes a period in her marriage that brought everything to the surface. What it revealed was not a broken relationship but two people who had never developed the language to say what they actually needed. That gap, between what is felt and what is spoken, is something seen consistently across decades of working with people in pain.

What is currently going unsaid in the relationship that matters most?

Comment RACHEL and I'll send you the full conversation.

#MarisaPeer #RachalPringle #Relationships #ConsciousCommunication #InnerWork
transcript: was a time in your marriage when you both had an open marriage. Yes. Can I ask you about that? What happened to lead you to that? I think the idea of threesomes and bringing another person in is a very common thing in relationship. At four years in, we actually really tried. He fell in love with someone else. I fell in love with someone else. It was an extreme catalyst, incredibly hurtful, and also the best thing that ever happened to us. We were both hiding behind a mask. We both didn't know how to speak what we really felt. Therefore, we were both missing something in each other, wanting more depth or more fire or more presence. We recognized that it was never worth destabilization of our relationship. And so through really a lot of heartache a lot of devastation a lot of pain we realized that we were the most important thing and that we wanted to come back together it created a really deep foundation of trust and safety and devotional love that now we get to live from
